# The Paving List

Marta had been caretaker at Hollowbrook Primary for twenty-three years, long enough to know which floorboards squeaked and which teachers cried in the supply closet. She knew the grounds the way you know an old friend's face—every weed, every bald patch of grass, every place where the rain pooled after a storm.

So when she found the first seedling, she noticed immediately.

It stood in the corner of the side yard, a spindly oak no taller than her boot, planted dead center in the area marked with orange spray paint. The paint was new. The contractors were coming in three weeks to lay the new parking lot—twelve spaces, staff only, approved by the council after two years of complaints about teachers parking on the residential streets.

Marta crouched and studied the seedling. The soil around it had been turned recently, watered even. Someone had taken care.

She should have pulled it out. The paving crew would grind it under regardless. But she'd watched the side yard shrink her whole career—the portables, the storage shed, the astroturf patch that replaced the wild corner where kids used to find beetles. She told herself she'd deal with it tomorrow.

The next week
